title: BIC/SWIFT Code Specification
description: Business Identifier Code (BIC) structure and validation rules. BIC (also known as SWIFT code) is the ISO 9362 standard for identifying financial institutions.

structure.description: BIC consists of 8 or 11 characters divided into 4 components

components.name: institution_code
components.description: Institution code (bank code) - 4 letters identifying the financial institution

components.name: country_code
components.description: Country code - ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code
components.validation: Must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code

components.name: location_code
components.description: Location code - identifies the city or location of the institution
components.notes: 0 in location code indicates test BIC (not for production use)

components.name: branch_code
components.description: Branch code - identifies a specific branch of the institution
conventions: When omitted, the BIC is 8 characters and refers to the head office
Branch codes are institution-specific and not standardized

8_character.description: 8-character BIC (BIC8) refers to the head office of the institution
8_character.usage: Used when referring to the institution as a whole or when the specific branch is not relevant
8_character.note: When processing, BIC8 can be treated as equivalent to BIC11 with 'XXX' branch

11_character.description: 11-character BIC (BIC11) identifies a specific branch of the institution
11_character.usage: Used when a specific branch must be identified in the transaction
11_character.note: If branch is 'XXX', it explicitly refers to the head office

validation_rules.description: BIC must be exactly 8 or 11 characters
Characters 1-4 must be uppercase letters A-Z
Characters 5-6 must be uppercase letters A-Z
Country code must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
validation_rules.validation: Must exist in countries.json reference data

validation_rules.description: Characters 7-8 must be uppercase letters A-Z or digits 0-9
Location code '0' in position 8 indicates a test BIC (not for production)
If present, characters 9-11 must be uppercase letters A-Z or digits 0-9
BIC must not contain spaces or special characters

invalid.reason: Too short - only 4 characters (missing country, location)
invalid.explanation: BIC must be 8 or 11 characters. This only contains the institution code.

invalid.reason: Too short - only 6 characters (missing location code)
invalid.explanation: BIC must be 8 or 11 characters. Country code present but location code missing.
BIC must be exactly 8 or 11 characters, not 9. Branch code is incomplete.
BIC must be exactly 8 or 11 characters, not 10. Branch code is incomplete.
BIC must use uppercase letters only. All alphabetic characters must be A-Z.

invalid.reason: Digits not allowed in institution code (positions 1-4)
invalid.explanation: Institution code must be 4 uppercase letters (A-Z). Digits are only allowed in location and branch codes.

invalid.reason: Digit not allowed in country code (positions 5-6)
invalid.explanation: Country code must be 2 uppercase letters matching ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format.
Country code must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. 'XX' is not assigned to any country.
BIC must be a continuous string without spaces or special characters.
BIC can only contain uppercase letters A-Z and digits 0-9. Hyphens and other special characters are not permitted.

invalid.reason: Underscores not allowed in branch code
invalid.explanation: Branch code must be alphanumeric (A-Z, 0-9). Underscores and other special characters are not permitted.

test_bics.description: BICs with '0' in position 8 of the location code are test BICs
test_bics.usage: Used in test and development environments only, not for production transactions

examples.description: Test BIC for Deutsche Bank, Germany
Test BIC for BNP Paribas, France

test_bics.validation: Production systems should reject or flag test BICs with warnings

head_office_convention.description: The branch code 'XXX' and omitted branch code both refer to the head office
head_office_convention.equivalence: BIC8 (e.g., DEUTDEFF) is equivalent to BIC11 with XXX branch (e.g., DEUTDEFFXXX)
head_office_convention.processing_rule: When comparing BICs, DEUTDEFF and DEUTDEFFXXX should be treated as identical
head_office_convention.normalization: Systems may normalize all BIC8 to BIC11 with 'XXX' appended for consistent processing

passive_participants.description: Some institutions are registered with SWIFT but are passive participants (receive only)
passive_participants.note: Passive participants can receive payments but cannot initiate them on the SWIFT network

common_mistakes.correction: Always use uppercase A-Z for all alphabetic characters
BIC is a continuous string with no separators
Only BIC8 and BIC11 are valid lengths

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming all banks have a BIC
common_mistakes.correction: Only institutions participating in the SWIFT network have BICs. Domestic-only banks may not have one.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using institution name instead of BIC code
common_mistakes.correction: Use the actual 8 or 11 character code, not the bank name
Country code must be a valid ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (check countries.json)
BIC identifies the institution, IBAN identifies an account at that institution

usage_notes: BIC is required in SWIFT MT messages (fields like 50A, 52A, 56A, 57A, etc.)
BIC is required in ISO 20022 MX messages (elements like DbtrAgt/FinInstnId/BICFI, CdtrAgt/FinInstnId/BICFI)
For SEPA Credit Transfers, BIC is optional if IBAN is provided (SEPA countries can route by IBAN alone)
For non-SEPA international payments, BIC is typically mandatory
When validating BICs, check against the SWIFT BIC Directory for active/registered codes
BICs can be deactivated or reassigned - always use current reference data
National Bank Codes (NBC) or Routing Numbers are NOT the same as BICs and cannot be used interchangeably
references: ISO 9362:2022 - Banking — Banking telecommunication messages — Business identifier code (BIC)
SWIFT BIC Directory (requires SWIFT membership for full access)
ISO 3166-1 - Codes for the representation of names of countries and their subdivisions
